A trade-wind trough oriented from the northwest to the southeast will
bring a brief wetter period of scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms tonight through Wednesday. Due to its orientation and 
northeasterly motion, Saipan and Tinian will see these showers 
first, with the onset this evening for their coastal waters, and 
after midnight for these islands. Remnant island-effect showers are 
ongoing for southwestern Guam and adjacent coastal waters, so a 
thunderstorm or two should not be ruled out from now until shortly 
after sunset. Then, isolated thunderstorms will become a concern for 
Guam and Rota after midnight, but the increase in shower coverage is 
not expected until Wednesday morning. The duration of these showers 
heavily depends on the longevity of this feature, however, model 
guidance indicates a return to drier weather starting Wednesday 
afternoon for Saipan and Tinian, and Wednesday evening for Guam and 
Rota. This along with slightly different wind directions out of the 
north and northeast supported a split zone, however, a return to one 
zone wouldn't be out of the question over these next few forecast 
issuances. Then, a potentially broad circulation may impact the 
region around Thursday, so shower coverage tops out at 30 percent, 
with thunderstorm potential most likely added in the coming shifts, 
but winds may be light and variable should the circulation remain 
weak. This situation will continue to be refined as confidence 
increases naturally with time. A return to drier weather is possible 
in the latter half of the week with isolated light showers (10% 
chance) included.

Marine...
Benign seas and light to gentle winds varying out of the north to
east are expected throughout the week. The zones remained split to
account for slight differences in wind directions and timing of
showers. A northeasterly trade swell will build in starting tonight,
eventually becoming the dominant pattern once the westerly swell
tapers down. There is a moderate risk of rip currents along west 
facing reefs tonight, joined by north and east facing reefs on 
Wednesday.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon surge is now affecting eastern Micronesia, with winds
increasing across Kosrae and showing strong signs of increasing over
Pohnpei by early Wednesday morning. The latest satellite data shows 
strong cumulus cloud lines moving rapidly through Kosrae. Convection 
looks to increase over Pohnpei and Kosrae through the night, with 
scattered showers expected at both locations by Wednesday morning. 
This looks to be the onset of a wet, unsettled pattern across both 
locations that looks to continue through the weekend. POPs 
(Probability of Precipitation) look to increase to around the 60 
percent range Thursday night at Pohnpei and Friday at Kosrae and 
continue at that level through the weekend. Models are indicating the
possibility of heavy rainfall potential, though confidence remains 
low at this time. Regardless, showers and thunderstorms are on tap 
for both locations through the weekend.

For Majuro, scattered showers are now in place across the waters 
just north of the atoll and only look to increase through the 
evening. POPs could reach the 60 percent range there as well
Wednesday night into Thursday as a weaker surge affects the
Marshalls, and again during the weekend.

For the marine forecast, winds have increased across Kosrae this
afternoon and look to increase across Pohnpei by Wednesday morning.
Fresh to strong monsoon winds in the surge are expected across
Pohnpei with moderate to fresh winds with frequent strong gusts 
across Kosrae. The surge looks to weaken by Thursday morning at
Kosrae and by Friday morning at Pohnpei. Based on winds, a Small
Craft Advisory was issued for Kosrae beginning this afternoon and 
for Pohnpei beginning early Thursday morning. Seas are not going to
be that impressive, but could reach as high as 7 to 8 feet at
Pohnpei, making for choppy seas in the open waters. For Kosrae, seas
are expected to be at or below 7 feet. Majuro looks to see gentle
winds increasing to moderate to fresh around Thursday afternoon.

Western Micronesia...
A ridge remains firmly in place over Palau and Yap regions, and is 
still inducing some diffluent flow, leading to quiet conditions over 
the several few days. During this period of drier weather, haze 
sourced from distant wildfires in Indonesia are expected to continue 
across Palau and Yap. Island-induced showers and thunderstorms are 
possible for Palau during the afternoons for the next few days. 
Overall, a fairly dry pattern is expected to remain through Sunday.
